issue_context.summary: FancyZones falls back to a default layout after a display dock is attached until PowerToys is restarted, instead of loading the saved layout for the new monitor configuration.
known_information: The original report uses PowerToys 0.67.1, Windows 11 22H2, a laptop panel, and a Samsung ultrawide.
Restarting PowerToys immediately restores the expected saved layouts.
No current-version confirmation or later discussion exists.
inferences: The hot-plug path may compute a transient monitor identity before EDID/serial information stabilizes, while startup computes the saved identity correctly.
issue_context.analysis: Current FancyZones has extensive monitor identity and work-area recreation logic, so a three-year-old package cannot establish whether the issue remains or which identity changes during hot-plug. A current package plus topology transition is the smallest discriminating evidence.
initial_investigation: FancyZones::ShouldWorkAreasBeRecreated compares monitor device ID, serial number, virtual desktop, and work-area rectangle.
Issue 8906 is a closed older monitor-configuration reset report; no linked fix for this issue was found.

comment.body:
Thanks for the clear dock attach sequence and for noting that a PowerToys restart immediately restores the saved layouts. The original 0.67.1 data predates substantial FancyZones monitor-identity changes, so the current hot-plug key must be compared with the startup key.

**Needed**
1. Please list each display's connection, resolution, scaling, orientation, primary status, and the exact dock attach/detach sequence on the latest stable build.
2. When the wrong default layout appears, please submit a comment containing `/bugreport` before restarting PowerToys.

This will show whether the hot-plug path sees a transient device/serial ID or fails to reload the matching applied layout.

proposed_fixes.title: Stabilize FancyZones applied-layout lookup after dock hot-plug
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Best current hypothesis: the hot-plug callback looks up layouts with a transient or incomplete monitor identity, falls back to default, and does not retry after identity stabilization.
plan: Log the full monitor identity and applied-layout key at each display-change phase.
Debounce/retry layout lookup until monitor identity stabilizes, without blocking the window event hook.
Preserve the last known layout per stable topology and add dock attach/detach integration coverage.
verification: Attach and detach the reported dock repeatedly and verify the saved per-topology layout loads without restarting PowerToys.

confidence.rationale: The restart behavior supports an identity timing issue, but no current trace confirms which key differs.
